newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr inches up, mostly shrugs off Japan trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr inches up, mostly shrugs off Japan trade data.

text.p: *0009 GMT --*Dollar edged higher against yen on buying from interbank traders and overseas operators, with traders mostly shrugging off data on Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus.
*Trade surplus rose 126.4 percent to 480.57 billion yen in first 20 days of July compared with year earlier.
*"The market is shrugging off the rise in the trade surplus, with many traders becoming bullish for the dollar," said a Japanese city bank trader.
*But sporadic selling by Japanese exporters and profit-taking capping dollar at around 119.50 yen, he added.
*MOF said surplus in same period a year earlier was 212.26 billion yen. Trade surplus in first 20 days of June stood at 453.20 billion yen.
*"There is a feeling that the surplus for July was not as large as for May and June," said a trust bank dealer.
*He said dollar likely to head higher, but expected to be capped below psychological resistance at 120 yen for Wednesday.
*The bank dealer said if dollar breaks through 120 yen, next resistance is seen at around 121.25/35 yen, which is 61.8 percent retracement between this year's low of 110.68 and highs of 127.47 yen.
